Hi Sam and Nina,

Thanks again for the productive demo yesterday. To get a precise Dedicated sizing estimate for NB-2027-0311, we need a short runbook and a small slice of telemetry. Can you send the following items (sample CSV or short doc is fine):

- 2 weeks of request-level telemetry (timestamp, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, latency_ms, response_code, customer_id or session_id if available)
- Typical concurrency at 95th and 99th percentiles (if you don't have percentiles, peak concurrent sessions and average concurrent sessions are OK)
- Common prompt/response token lengths (median, 90th, 99th) and whether you use long-system prompts or many short prompts per call
- Expected SLOs (p50/p95 latency targets) and acceptable cold-start windows
- Mix of workloads (chat vs. single-turn generation vs. embeddings/rerank) and any scheduled batch jobs/cron inference

If you have an existing runbook (or a short architecture diagram showing any frontend queuing, session affinity, or caching), attach it and we can fold it into our sizing. I attached a one-page template (nebula_requirements_runbook.docx) you can fill quickly.

Goal: get to a preliminary GPU footprint + burst plan this week so we can lock capacity pricing and SLA window.

Thanks,

Priya — attaching a scrubbed sample of our telemetry and a short internal runbook. High-level notes below and the CSV is attached (nebula_sample_telemetry.csv).

Quick summary:
- 2-week sample (Mar 1–14) captured at our API gateway (per-request). We removed user PII and token-level content.
- Traffic shape: steady baseline ~120 qps, daily spikes to ~650 qps (US business hours), and a weekly marketing batch at 02:00 UTC that creates a ~20-minute burst to ~1,200 qps once per week.
- Concurrency: 95th ~480 concurrent inference requests, 99th ~820. These values count active requests, not sessions.
- Prompt/response: median prompt 60 tokens, median completion 140 tokens. 90th prompt 220 / completion 560. 99th prompt 1,200 / completion 2,000 (long retrieval + summarize jobs).
- Workload mix: ~70% multi-turn chat (state kept in client), 20% single-turn batch summarization, 10% embeddings/rerank. Embedding calls are short and CPU-heavy on our side.
- Cache: we have a client-side prefix cache with a hit rate ~12% for repeated prompts; server-side KV cache is not in use today.
- Affinity: sticky session tokens for conversational flows (session affinity at LB layer).
- Preferred SLO: p95 < 600ms for chat, but we are willing to accept p95 < 1,200ms for some long summarization jobs.

Attachments: nebula_sample_telemetry.csv, nebula_requirements_runbook.docx

Let us know if you want more granular telemetry (e.g., per-model shards, error-level breakdown). Happy to hop on a quick call.

—Sam

- Burst plan to handle 1,200 qps weekly marketing spike (can we achieve >50% of burst with rapid autoscale + queued traffic?)

Sam/Nina: two quick clarifying Qs we couldn't infer from the CSV — can you confirm the following?
1) Are the 99th percentile long jobs mostly single-turn (batch summarization) or multi-turn flows that incrementally grow to 2k tokens?
2) Do you have a preferred model family (open-vicuna-style vs. Llama-based variants) you plan to serve or are you expecting Redwood to recommend a variant?

I'll pull a draft estimate and a short runbook template we can send back.

Thanks,
Priya

Thanks for the sample — good detail. Preliminary sizing notes and assumptions below. I'll produce a formal estimate (redwood-dedicated-estimate-v2.pdf) after we confirm a couple of behavioral points.

Assumptions:
- Target model: Llama-variant tuned for multi-turn; assume 16k context. We'll present two profiles: 1) latency-first (fp16 + int8 for some layers) and 2) cost-first (aggressive int8/4-bit quant).
- Average tokens per request (weighted by mix): ~200 tokens. Peak heavy jobs weigh on memory (2k completions).
- Typical batch size: continuous streaming with small dynamic batching (most requests are chat so batch sizes average 8–12).
- Cache: recommend enabling server-side KV cache with a 20–30% effective hit rate for prefix/cacheable summarization tasks — we can achieve this by adding a small redis-backed KV on the serving tier.

Prelim GPU footprint (very rough):
- Baseline: 8 x A100-80GB (or equivalent AMPere family) to meet steady 120 qps with p95 < 600ms, assuming optimized kernel selection and continuous batching.
- Scale zone for daily spikes: autoscale pool to +6 GPUs to cover 650 qps target headroom.
- Burst capacity plan: for the 1,200 qps weekly event, recommend a reserved burst pool of 6–10 GPUs (or cross-region fallback). We can also accept queued tail latency for batch summarization (if Nebula prefers cost savings).

Memory / KV considerations: the 2k completion jobs will require higher KV cache memory per GPU and we should ensure model shard placement allows >2k context without excessive OOM. Recommend 80GB+ GPU memory per replica or model partitioning.

Clarifying Qs for Nebula: (can you reply inline)
1) Are most of the 2k-token jobs single-shot batch summarization or multi-turn sessions?
2) What is your preferred availability for the 20-minute weekly marketing spike: do you need hard SLOs during the spike or can those jobs be queued/backfilled?
3) Any constraints on using server-side Redis (managed by you) vs. Redwood-managed cache?

I'll prepare the estimate doc and a short runbook explaining autoscale triggers, cache sizing, and rollback/fallback policy.

Thanks, team — this is very helpful. Quick answers inline and next steps below.

On Thu, Mar 11, 2027 at 09:47 AM Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.dev> wrote:
> Clarifying Qs for Nebula:
> 1) Are most of the 2k-token jobs single-shot batch summarization or multi-turn sessions?

Most of the 2k completions are single-shot summarization of long documents (we ship long docs to the model as a single prompt after retrieval). We do see a small number (maybe 5–8% of those cases) of multi-turn conversions that happen to grow large, but they are rare.

> 2) What is your preferred availability for the 20-minute weekly marketing spike: do you need hard SLOs during the spike or can those jobs be queued/backfilled?

We prefer soft SLOs during the marketing burst — it's acceptable for long summarization jobs to be queued up to 3 minutes, but chat traffic should remain responsive (p95 under 1s ideally).

> 3) Any constraints on using server-side Redis (managed by you) vs. Redwood-managed cache?

We can provision a managed Redis in our cloud account (AWS). We prefer Redwood to provide sizing guidance rather than host the cache.

Next steps:
- We can do a 30-minute call Mon 15 Mar to review the formal estimate and runbook.
- We'll also grant a short-lived HubSpot share (link above) and can upload a slightly longer telemetry slice if useful.

Thanks — Nina
